唐乾寧元年十二月二十六日

title.en: acting Minister of Works and military governor of Lulong Army at Youzhou
title.zh: 檢校司空、幽州廬龍軍節度使

claims.statement: prophesied to receive military commission at age forty-nine

sourceDate.text: 八月十三日，守光僭號大燕皇帝

claims.assessment: vulgar and dull by nature; increasingly cruel

kinshipTerm.en: grandfather of Zhi / father of Qian

held the far south amid Central Plains turmoil
usurped false title after ruined state

translationRepairs: On the twenty-sixth Kuangchou abandoned the city and fled. The Prince sent Li Cun'an and Rengong into Youzhou to calm the populace and seal the treasury, then appointed Rengong military governor of Youzhou, leaving a dozen trusted men including Yan Liude to share civil and military duties before returning himself.

On the twenty-sixth Kuangchou abandoned the city and fled. The Prince sent Li Cunshen and Rengong into Youzhou to calm the populace and seal the treasury, then appointed Rengong military governor of Youzhou, leaving a dozen trusted men including Yan Liude to share civil and military duties before returning himself.
李存審 is Li Cunshen; the current Cun'an does not match either the characters or their reading.
On the fifth of the ninth month he halted at Anseijun.
On the fifth of the ninth month he halted at Anse Army.
安塞軍 is Anse Army; Anseijun leaves 軍 fused and untranslated.

In the third month of the first year of Guanghua (898) he sent his eldest son to seize Luzhou; Lu Yanwei abandoned the city and fled. Rengong then held Cang, Jing, and De, installed Shouwen as acting governor, and petitioned the court for the command baton.

In the third month of the first year of Guanghua (898) he sent his eldest son to seize Cangzhou; Lu Yanwei abandoned the city and fled. Rengong then held Cang, Jing, and De, installed Shouwen as acting governor, and petitioned the court for the command baton.
Lu Yanwei held Cangzhou, and the same sentence immediately lists 滄 among the acquired prefectures. Parallel text confirms 滄州, not Luzhou.

From the seventh month through the tenth Rengong sent more than a hundred envoys begging Jin for aid. The Prince then called on Yan for troops; Rengong sent his commanders Li Pu and Xia Houjing, overseer Zhang Juhua, secretary Ma Yu, and others with thirty thousand men to join the campaign.

From the seventh month through the tenth Rengong sent more than a hundred envoys begging Jin for aid. The Prince then called on Yan for troops; Rengong sent his commanders Li Pu and Xiahou Jing, overseer Zhang Juhan, secretary Ma Yu, and others with thirty thousand men to join the campaign.
夏侯 is the compound surname Xiahou, and 張居翰 is Zhang Juhan; both current English forms are incorrect.
